terra.problem: The cookie jar comparison shifts from trusting wealth to wealth running out. The psalm does not say their riches will run out, and the comparison does not match the action.
The baker who works on a batch without getting a crumb does not match the psalm’s picture of people leaving wealth to others when they die.
The psalm says the lands were their namesakes, not that the people named the lands after themselves.
The claim that the grand house does not last forever is not stated in the psalm.
The explanation makes having riches without understanding the cause of the man’s fate. The psalm compares such a man to beasts that perish; it does not state that cause.
